candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP request target path (and query string), controlled by any unauthenticated client reaching the esigate filter: e.g. GET /<mapping-prefix>/http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal admin URL. Because selectProvider() uses the decoded URI path, percent-encoded forms such as %3A%2F%2F also decode to '://' before stripping.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that DriverRequest.external is only true for strings starting with literal 'http://'/'https://' (UriUtils.isAbsolute, UriUtils.java:310-312), that relative URLs are otherwise rewritten to the provider/firstBaseURL host (HttpClientRequestExecutor.java:232-240), that redirect handling re-maps external redirects back to the provider for non-external requests (FragmentRedirectStrategy), and that selectProvider itself does not validate the stripped relativeUri. Checked that stripMappingPath defaults to false (Parameters.java:49) - so deployments without it are not affected - but the project's shipped sample configs enable it, and that DriverFactoryTest/UriMapping only assert prefix stripping without any scheme/host validation. Also verified that ResourceUtilsTest.testGetHttpUrlWithQueryStringAbsoluteurl documents absolute-URL pass-through as intended API behavior and that DriverTest.testForwardCookiesExternalUrl exercises direct absolute-URL proxy calls, which is why the flaw is scoped to absolute URLs derived from the untrusted request path rather than the ResourceUtils API itself.
candidates.impact: A remote client can make ESIGate perform arbitrary outbound HTTP(S) requests with attacker-chosen method/body and read the full response, enabling access to internal-only services, cloud metadata endpoints and loopback/admin interfaces, plus internal port/host probing. The proxied response is returned to the client, so this is a full read SSRF, not blind. Configured extensions may also attach request headers to the outgoing request (e.g. X-Forwarded-For/X_REMOTE_USER via RemoteUserAuthenticationHandler).
candidates.prerequisites: A driver with stripMappingPath=true and a mapping with a non-null path prefix that the crafted path satisfies (this combination is used throughout the project's own sample configurations, e.g. esigate-app-aggregator/src/main/resources/esigate.properties uses /ag2/* and /nocache/ag1/* with stripMappingPath=true), and a servlet container that passes the crafted path through to the filter (raw request URI containing either the literal 'http://' segment or encoded %2F%2F; the literal form only requires the container not to normalize it away, while encoded-slash forms depend on the container's allowEncodedSlash-equivalent setting, which is a limitation noted below).
candidates.root_cause: In proxy mode the target URL is derived from the untrusted request path without verifying it is still a relative URL. DriverFactory.selectProvider() takes requestURI.getPath() (decoded percent-escapes) and, when the driver has stripMappingPath=true and the matched mapping has a path prefix, DriverFactory.stripMappingPath() removes that prefix leaving a value such as "http://internal-host/". DriverRequest then computes external = UriUtils.isAbsolute(relUrl) (DriverRequest.java:54), ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString() keeps the absolute URL unchanged (ResourceUtils.java:67-81), and HttpClientRequestExecutor.createOutgoingRequest() extracts physicalHost from that URL and skips the provider rewrite because external=true (HttpClientRequestExecutor.java:227-241), so the request is physically sent to the attacker-chosen host instead of the configured provider.
candidates.title: SSRF via request path treated as absolute URL in proxy mode (stripMappingPath)
candidates.trace: 1) Client sends GET /<prefix>/http://internal-host/... (or /<prefix>/http%3A%2F%2Finternal-host/...). 2) ProxyFilter -> RequestFactory.create builds the IncomingRequest request line from request.getRequestURI() (esigate-servlet/.../RequestFactory.java:54-59). 3) DriverFactory.selectProvider (DriverFactory.java:243-277) parses it with UriUtils.createURI and takes requestURI.getPath(), which decodes %3A/%2F, then calls stripMappingPath when isStripMappingPath() is true (line 270-272), producing 'http://internal-host/...'. 4) Driver.proxy builds DriverRequest(relUrl) (Driver.java:270-294); DriverRequest sets external=true (DriverRequest.java:54). 5) ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString leaves the absolute URL untouched (ResourceUtils.java:68-74) and appends the client query string. 6) HttpClientRequestExecutor.createOutgoingRequest extracts physicalHost from the attacker URL and, because isExternal() is true, does not rewrite the URI to the configured provider (HttpClientRequestExecutor.java:230-241). 7) Driver.requestExecutor.execute sends the HTTP request to the attacker/internal host and the upstream response (including body and status) is returned to the client through the normal proxy path (Driver.java:298-315, ResponseSender).
candidates.unverified: Exploitability was NOT runtime-confirmed. Two conditions could not be validated statically: (a) whether specific servlet containers pass a path containing a literal 'http://' segment through to the filter vs. normalizing/400-rejecting it, and (b) whether containers allow the percent-encoded variant (%3A%2F%2F), since Tomcat rejects encoded slashes by default. The source-level trust chain is complete, but the attack requires a container/config combination that meets these conditions; the mapping must also have a path prefix with stripMappingPath enabled.

coverage_summary: Coverage is based on the 426 model-visible files reported by get_source_scope (427 source-root files; 1 excluded by sensitive-name/path filter, 0 symlinks, 0 over the size cap; binary-like files are refused/skipped). The P1 index is partial: 316 Java files parsed, 136 files omitted, 0 parse errors, with syntax-only containment/call/inheritance candidates and no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution or reachability proof (9724 call sites, 6960 unresolved). I inspected the main runtime paths end-to-end: esigate-servlet entry (ProxyFilter, RequestFactory, ResponseSender, ResponseCapturingWrapper, ServletExtension, ConnectorFilter/FilteredRequest), esigate-core driver/proxy/render flow (Driver, DriverFactory, DriverConfiguration, DriverRequest, UriMapping, IndexedInstances, ResourceUtils, UriUtils, UrlRewriter, HttpClientRequestExecutor, ProxyingHttpClientBuilder, HeaderManager, IncomingRequest/OutgoingRequest, HttpErrorPage, cookie manager), ESI and parallel-ESI processing (EsiRenderer, IncludeElement, InlineElement/InlineCache, VarsElement/VariablesResolver, Fragment/Replace/Try/Choose/When elements, Tag/Parser), aggregation/template tags, extensions (Esi, Aggregate, ResourceFixup, Surrogate, ErrorPages, ConfigReload*, FetchLogging/FragmentLogging, XPoweredBy, DNS), cache storages, esigate-cas and esigate-server (ControlHandler is bound to 127.0.0.1), plus the unit/integration test suites that pin intended behavior. Sample application modules (esigate-app-*) and site XML were skimmed for configuration evidence (stripMappingPath=true with path mappings is the shipped norm). Items not reviewed in depth: the Future/parallel parser internals, monitoring/metrics plumbing, site documentation details, and the CAS/Spring demo application configuration.
limitations: Static review only: no code execution, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were run; no runtime confirmation of any finding.

The P1 relation index is partial and syntax-based (no control/data-flow, no semantic resolution, 6960 unresolved call sites, 136 omitted files); index edges were treated as navigation hints and every reported chain was verified against source text.

Exploitability of the SSRF candidate depends on servlet-container path handling (literal '//' vs percent-encoded %2F) and on stripMappingPath=true with a path mapping; these environmental conditions could not be validated in this run.

The submission cap is one candidate; other plausible but weaker/conditional leads (global InlineCache, ESI stylesheet fetch, CAS ticket handling, X-Forwarded-* spoofing) are documented as rejected/unconfirmed leads rather than separate candidates, so their absence from candidates is not a statement that they are safe.
Sample/demo applications and their configurations (esigate-app-*, esigate-war, esigate-app-casified-*) were reviewed only for configuration and test evidence, not as production code.
No external data (CVE/CWE lookups, upstream fix commits, sibling versions or runtime ground truth) was used; the vulnerability type/name is an analytical classification.

rejected_leads.lead: X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto spoofing: HeaderManager.copyHeaders appends the socket remote address to a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and keeps a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto (HeaderManager.java:123-145).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented and pinned as intended behavior by tests (XForwardedHeadersTest asserts '192.168.0.1, 127.0.0.1' and retention of client X-Forwarded-Proto) and by the reference documentation; the downstream consumer is expected to discard the left-most, untrusted values.

rejected_leads.lead: Static, process-global InlineCache shared across requests/users: esi/InlineCache.java and extension/parallelesi/InlineCache.java use a static HashMap keyed only by the esi:inline name, store fragments with outdate=null (never expiring), ignore the stored 'fetchable' flag, and InlineElement stores fragments that any later esi:include with the same name is served from IncludeElement.processPage (esi/IncludeElement.java:184-188).
rejected_leads.reason: Real source-level concerns (cross-request fragment disclosure/poisoning and unbounded growth) but the security impact depends on a provider page placing user-specific content inside esi:inline and on how the owner scopes fragment names; no CVE/fix evidence and the component behavior looks like the (poorly scoped) intended caching implementation. Left as an unconfirmed lead, not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: esi:include 'stylesheet' attribute: IncludeElement.processPage fetches the XSLT via driver.render(xslt, ...) and XsltRenderer builds a Transformer from it (esi/IncludeElement.java:199-203, xml/XsltRenderer.java:70-97) without FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING or external-access restrictions.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an attacker to inject ESI tags into content served by the provider (reflection scenario); without that precondition this is template-author controlled. Not independently verifiable from this snapshot and not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: CasAuthenticationHandler.isRedirectToCasServer uses a substring 'contains(loginUrl)' test on the provider Location header and then re-sends the request with a CAS proxy ticket appended to the outgoing URI (CasAuthenticationHandler.java:49-67, 118-127).
rejected_leads.reason: The ticket is appended to the URI that was already chosen for the request, and exploitation would require an attacker-controlled redirect response plus an installed CAS extension; the chain is too conditional and the esigate-cas extension is optional. Left as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: HttpRequestHelper.getHost parses the client-supplied Host header with split(':')/Integer.parseInt (HttpRequestHelper.java:64-81) and is used when preserveHost=true; malformed values (e.g. non-numeric or IPv6-bracket ports) raise NumberFormatException.
rejected_leads.reason: At most a per-request error/DoS and depends on the container forwarding malformed Host values; no security-relevant state change. Rejected as too weak.

summary:
ESIGate 5.3-SNAPSHOT multi-module Java web aggregator/ESI processor. Reviewed the servlet entry chain (ProxyFilter -> RequestFactory -> DriverFactory), the driver/proxy/render core, URL/resource handling, HTTP client execution, header/cookie managers, ESI and parallel-ESI parsers and elements (include/inline/vars), aggregation/template tags, Surrogate/cache extensions, CAS and standalone-server modules, plus test evidence.

Strongest distinct candidate: Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918) in proxy mode. Incoming request paths are derived from the raw servlet request URI and decoded with java.net.URI#getPath(); when a driver is configured with stripMappingPath=true and a path mapping, the mapping prefix is stripped and the remainder is trusted as a "relative" URL. A path such as `/ag2/http://attacker-or-internal-host/...` therefore yields `http://attacker-or-internal-host/...`, which DriverRequest marks as external, ResourceUtils keeps as an absolute URL, and HttpClientRequestExecutor fetches from the attacker-chosen host (physicalHost is extracted from that URI and the URI is not rewritten back to the configured provider when external). The response is proxied back to the client, giving a full SSRF read primitive to arbitrary hosts/internal services.

Other plausible leads were reviewed but rejected or left unconfirmed (X-Forwarded-For spoofing is documented/tested intended behavior; global static InlineCache; ESI include `stylesheet` XSLT fetch; CAS ticket append), and are not submitted as separate candidates.
